'''Aleksej Pokuševski''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Алексеј Покушевски}}; born 26 December 2001) is a Serbian professional [[basketball]] player for [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]] of the [[VTB United League]]. Standing at {{height|ft=7|in=0}} and weighing {{convert|210|lb|0}}, he plays at the [[power forward]] position.

Born in [[Belgrade]], Pokuševski was previously a youth player for the Greek club [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]]. He debuted for their senior team in 2018, at age 17 and becoming the youngest [[EuroLeague]] player in club history. He was selected by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] with the 17th overall pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]] and traded to the Thunder.

==Early career==
Pokuševski grew up in [[Novi Sad]], where he started to play youth basketball for local clubs, KK Kadet, KK NS Stars and [[KK Vojvodina|Vojvodina]]. In 2015, Pokuševski joined the [[youth system]] of [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]]. In 2017, he participated in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] camp. In August 2018, he attended the [[Basketball Without Borders]] Europe camp, in [[Belgrade]], Serbia.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jokic, Vucevic Headline Basketball Without Borders Europe 2018 |url=http://global.nba.com/news/jokic-vucevic-headline-basketball-without-borders-europe-2018/ |website=global.nba.com |access-date=20 March 2019}}</ref> In February 2019, Pokuševski was invited for the [[NBA All-Star]] Basketball Without Borders Global Camp in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]], but eventually missed the event after being rejected for a [[U.S. visa]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2019 NBA All-Stars Nikola Jokić and Nikola Vučević, Deandre Ayton and Bogdan Bogdanović to coach top international prospects at fifth annual Basketball Without Borders Camp |url=https://pr.nba.com/bwb-global-camp-2019-all-star/ |website=pr.nba.com |date=12 February 2019 |access-date=20 March 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Olympiacos (2019–2020)===
On 19 March 2019, Pokuševski made his [[EuroLeague]] debut with [[Olympiacos BC|Olympiacos]], in a 89–69 win over the German club [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]], during the EuroLeague's [[2018–19 EuroLeague|2018–19 season]]. He recorded 1 point, 2 rebounds and 1 assist, in one minute played during the game.<ref>{{cite web |title=2018-19 Regular Season Round 27 Olympiacos Piraeus 89 - 69 FC Bayern Munich |url=https://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=211&seasoncode=E2018#!boxscore |website=euroleague.net |access-date=20 March 2019}}</ref> Pokuševski became the youngest senior men's Olympiacos player to ever debut in the EuroLeague. At 17 years and 83 days old, he replaced [[Georgios Printezis]], who had previously debuted in the EuroLeague, at the age of 17 years and 229 days, as the club's youngest-ever EuroLeague player.<ref>{{cite web |title=Aleksej Pokusevski became youngest ever Olympiacos player to debut in EuroLeague |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/847137/aleksej-pokusevski-became-youngest-ever-olympiacos-player-to-debut-in-euroleague/ |website=eurohoops.net |date=19 March 2019 |access-date=20 March 2019}}</ref>

For the [[2019–20 Greek A2 Basket League|2019–20 season]], Pokuševski was assigned to play in the [[Greek A2 Basket League|Greek A2 League]], the country's second-tier league, with Olympiacos' [[reserve team]], [[Olympiacos BC B Development Team|Olympiacos B]]. He initially played for the senior EuroLeague club's [[practice squad]]. During the season, Pokuševski missed almost 3 months of playing time, due to a [[knee injury]].<ref>[https://stats.nba.com/articles/2020-nba-draft-profile-Aleksej-Pokusevski/ 2020 NBA Draft Profile: Aleksej Pokusevski.]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://advanceprobasketball.com/2020/05/06/aleksej-pokusevski-scouting-report-by-zachary-smith/ |title=Aleksej Pokusevski Injury History. |access-date=15 September 2020 |archive-date=23 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210123110500/https://advanceprobasketball.com/2020/05/06/aleksej-pokusevski-scouting-report-by-zachary-smith/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Pokuševski started in eight of his 11 appearances in the Greek A2, averaging 10.8 points, 7.9 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.8 blocks in 23.1 minutes per game. He shot 40.4 percent from the field, 32.1 percent from three-point range, and 78.3 percent from the free-throw line.<ref>[https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Aleksej-Pokusevski/Summary/130811 International Regular Season Stats - Per Game.]</ref> In the middle of the season, Olympiacos' main EuroLeague team was riddled with injuries, and Pokuševski was called up to the senior team. He played two minutes in his only EuroLeague game of the season,<ref>[https://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=008232&seasoncode=E2019 POKUSEVSKI, ALEKSEJ OLYMPIACOS PIRAEUS EuroLeague 2019-20 STATISTICS.]</ref> before the league's season was suspended due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]].

On 24 April 2020, Pokuševski declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=25 April 2020 |title=Serbian forward Aleksej Pokusevski declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29094835 |access-date=22 March 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Pokuševski was under contract with [[Olympiacos BC|Olympiacos]] through the end of the 2023–24 season. The contract's [[buyout clause]] for the [[NBA]] was €1 million if he was a top-20 [[NBA draft|draft]] pick, or €1.5 million if he was a top-14 [[lottery pick]].<ref>[https://www.novasports.gr/the-experts/article/1761085/o-%E2%80%98%E2%80%99pokou%E2%80%99%E2%80%99-fernei-zesto-xrima-sto-tameio-tou-olumpiakou O ‘’Ποκού’’ φέρνει ζεστό χρήμα στο ταμείο του Ολυμπιακού! {{in lang|it}}.]</ref><ref>[https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1053853/aleksej-pokusevskis-nba-buyout-may-reportedly-near-1-5m/ Aleksej Pokusevski's NBA buyout may reportedly near 1.5M.]</ref> Following selection in the NBA draft, Pokuševski left Olympiacos on 24 November 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pokuševski se oprostio od Olimpijakosa (VIDEO) |url=https://www.mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/pokusevski-se-oprostio-od-olimpijakosa-video/371528 |website=mozzartsport.com |access-date=24 November 2020}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2020–2024)===
On November 18, 2020, Pokuševski was selected with the 17th overall pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], becoming the youngest player selected that year.<ref>{{cite web|first=Joseph|last=Salvador|title=NBA draft 2020: Five things to know about Aleksej Pokusevski, taken 17th overall by the Timberwolves|url=https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/2020/11/18/aleksej-pokusevski-minnesota-timberwolves-2020-nba-draft/3764405001/|website=USAToday.com|date=18 November 2020|access-date=19 November 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Moke|last=Hamilton|title='It was perfect': Rookie Aleksej Pokusevski excited to be in OKC|url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2020/12/03/it-was-perfect-rookie-aleksej-pokusevski-excited-to-be-in-okc/|website=USAToday.com|date=3 December 2020|access-date=26 March 2021}}</ref> Two days later, his draft rights were sent to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in a three-team trade<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Acquires Draft Rights to Aleksej Pokuševski, James Johnson and 2024 Second-Round Draft Pick|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/pokusevski-johnson-201120|website=NBA.com|date=20 November 2020|access-date=21 November 2020}}</ref> and on 9 December, he signed with the Thunder,<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Aleksej Pokuševski|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/pokusevski-201209|website=NBA.com|date=9 December 2020|access-date=9 December 2020}}</ref> becoming the [[List of oldest and youngest National Basketball Association players|youngest active player in the NBA]] that season.<ref>{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Nilon|title=OKC Thunder: Aleksej Pokusevski viewed as a 'player to watch' in fantasy|url=https://thunderousintentions.com/2021/03/18/okc-thunder-aleksej-pokusevski-watch/|website=ThunderousIntentions.com|date=18 March 2021|access-date=26 March 2021}}</ref> On 3 February 2021, Pokuševski received his first assignment at the [[Oklahoma City Blue]], the Thunder's affiliate team in the [[NBA G League]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Assigns Four to Blue|url=https://oklahomacity.gleague.nba.com/news/thunder-assigns-four-to-blue|website=NBA.com|date=3 February 2021|access-date=3 February 2021}}</ref> and on 14 March, he made his first NBA career start where he scored 23 points, including five 3-pointers, grabbed a career-high 10 rebounds and dished out 4 assists in a 128–122 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], becoming the third Thunder rookie (following [[Russell Westbrook]] and [[Darius Bazley]]) to post a 20–10 double-double. At 19 years and 78 days old, he became the youngest player in franchise history to score 20-plus points while also setting the record for being the youngest player in league history with 20-plus points, 10-plus rebounds and 5-plus three-pointers made in a game. Pokuševski also became the second-youngest player in NBA history to make five three-pointers in a game behind only [[LeBron James]] in 2004.<ref>{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Gallo|title=By the Numbers: Thunder Comes Back, Poku Soars|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/story/btn-grizzlies-210314|website=NBA.com|date=14 March 2021|access-date=15 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Logan|last=Newman|title=Poku's double-double, 3-point barrage leads Thunder over Grizzlies|url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2021/03/14/aleksej-pokusevski-double-double-3-pointers-thunder-beat-grizzlies/|website=USAToday.com|date=14 March 2021|access-date=15 March 2021}}</ref>

On April 3, 2022, Pokuševski recorded his first NBA [[triple-double]] with 17 points, 10 rebounds, and 12 assists in a 117–96 win over the [[2021–22 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Tony|last=Sellars|title=WITH BOOKER RESTING, SARR, POKUVESKI LEAD THUNDER PAST SUNS|url=https://www.nba.com/game/phx-vs-okc-0022101174|website=NBA.com|date=3 April 2022|access-date=4 April 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Prvi tripl-dabl u NBA karijeri Alekseja Pokuševskog|url=https://mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/prvi-tripl-dabl-u-nba-karijeri-alekseja-pokusevskog-video/416613|website=MozzartSport.com|date=4 April 2022|access-date=4 April 2022|language=sr}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Aleksej Pokusevski surprises with triple-double as Thunder rout Suns|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/basketball-nba-okc-phx-idUSMTZXEI44SKO6CO|website=Reuters.com|date=4 April 2022|access-date=4 April 2022}}</ref> becoming the seventh Thunder and the 12th-youngest player in NBA history (after [[Magic Johnson]]) to achieve a triple-double.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pokuševski tik iza velikog Medžika Džonsona|url=https://mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/pokusevski-tik-iza-velikog-medzika-dzonsona/416634|website=MozzartSport.com|date=4 April 2022|access-date=4 April 2022|language=sr}}</ref> Pokuševski made 61 appearances (12 starts) for the Thunder during the [[2021–22 NBA season]], averaging 7.6 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 2.1 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Aleksej Pokusevski 2021–22 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4683018/type/nba/year/2022|access-date=March 7, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

In July 2022, Pokuševski joined the Thunder for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Oklahoma City Thunder 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612760/thunder|website=NBA.com|access-date=9 July 2022}}</ref> On November 22, Pokuševski scored 16 points and grabbed 14 rebounds during a 126–122 loss to the [[2022–23 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Doug|last=Alden|title=SMART HELPS CELTICS BEAT THUNDER FOR 7TH STRAIGHT WIN|url=https://www.nba.com/game/okc-vs-bos-0022200201|website=NBA.com|date=15 November 2022|access-date=15 November 2022}}</ref> From December 2022 to March 2023, Pokuševski was unable to play due to a non-displaced [[tibial plateau fracture]] in his left leg.<ref>{{cite web|first=Rylan|last=Stiles|title=Aleksej Pokusevski sees first game action since December|url=https://thunderousintentions.com/2023/03/15/aleksej-pokusevski-returns-game-injury/|website=ThunderousIntentions.com|date=15 March 2023|access-date=15 March 2023}}</ref> He made 34 appearances (including 25 starts) for Oklahoma City during the [[2022–23 NBA season|2022–23 season]], averaging 8.1 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 1.9 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Aleksej Pokusevski 2022–23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4683018/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=March 7, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

Pokuševski appeared in 10 games for Oklahoma City in the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24 season]], posting averages of 1.2 points, 1.0 rebound, and 0.5 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Aleksej Pokusevski 2023–24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4683018/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=March 7, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> On 23 February 2024, Pokuševski was waived by the Thunder.<ref>{{cite web|title=THUNDER WAIVES POKUŠEVSKI|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-pokusevski-240223|website=NBA.com|date=23 February 2024|access-date=23 February 2024}}</ref>

===Charlotte Hornets (2024)===
On 28 February 2024, Pokuševski signed with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets Sign Aleksej Pokusevski|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-sign-aleksej-pokusevski|website=NBA.com|date=28 February 2024|access-date=28 February 2024}}</ref> Pokuševski made 18 appearances for the Hornets, recording averages of 7.4 points, 4.4 rebounds, and 1.7 assists. On 6 July, he was waived by Charlotte.<ref>{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Waive Davis Bertans, Bryce McGowens and Aleksej Pokusevski|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-waive-davis-bertans-bryce-mcgowens-and-aleksej-pokusevski|website=NBA.com|date=6 July 2024|access-date=14 July 2024}}</ref>

===Partizan (2024–2026)===
On 20 August 2024, Pokuševski signed with [[KK Partizan|Partizan Mozzart Bet]] of the [[ABA League]], [[Basketball League of Serbia]] (KLS) and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Crno-bela simfonija: Nova energija i duh tradicije Partizana na ulasku u sezonu 2024-25|url=https://partizan.basketball/vesti/aktuelno/3738|website=Partizan.basketball|date=20 August 2024|access-date=20 August 2024|language=Serbian |last1=Normasoft. Net |first1=Normasoft }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Geoff|last=Gillingham|title=Aleksej Pokusevski seals move to Partizan|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/aleksej-pokusevski-seals-move-to-kk-partizan/|website=EuroLeagueBasketball.net|date=19 August 2024|access-date=19 August 2024}}</ref> In his debut season with Partizan, Pokuševski averaged 3.9 points and 2.2 rebounds over 27 EuroLeague games. During the 2024–25 season, Partizan managed to lift the record eighth [[2024–25 ABA League First Division|ABA League]] championship, and the [[2024–25 Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]] championship, the first one after 11 seasons. On 21 July 2026, the team did not activate the additional year included in his contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Former NBA first-round pick officially leaves Partizan |url=https://basketnews.com/news-252390-aleksej-pokusevski-leaves-partizan-after-club-declines-contract-option.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=24 July 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

===Lokomotiv Kuban (2026–present)===
On 6 August 2026, Pokuševski signed with [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]] of the [[VTB United League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=👋 Добро пожаловать, Алексей!|url=https://lokobasket.com/news/362549/|website=lokobasket.com|date=6 August 2026|access-date=7 August 2026|language=ru}}</ref>

==National team career==
Pokuševski was a member of the [[Serbia men's national under-17 basketball team|Serbian national under-17 team]] that competed at the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 World Cup]], in [[Argentina]]. Over seven tournament games, he averaged 7.7 points, 8.3 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 3.0 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Aleksej POKUSEVSKI at the 2018 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2018/player/Aleksej-Pokusevski |website=fiba.basketball |access-date=20 March 2019}}</ref>

Pokuševski was a member of the [[Serbia men's national under-18 basketball team|Serbian national under-18 team]] that competed at the [[2019 FIBA Under-18 European Championship]], in [[Volos]], Greece. Over seven tournament games, he averaged 10.0 points, 7.2 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 2.7 steals and 4.0 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=2019 Serbia U18 - Pokusevski |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2019/player/Aleksej-Pokusevski |website=fiba.basketball |access-date=8 August 2019}}</ref>

Initially at the preliminary [[2022 Serbia EuroBasket team|Serbia roster]] for [[EuroBasket 2022]], Pokuševski was cut from the squad due to disapproval of the Thunder.<ref name="Poku-Jov">{{cite web |title=Problemi za Srbiju: Majami i Oklahoma nisu pustili Jovića i Pokuševskog |url=https://mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/problemi-za-srbiju-majami-i-oklahoma-nisu-pustili-jovica-i-pokusevskog/426827 |website=mozzartsport.com |access-date=3 August 2022}}</ref><ref name="Poku-Jov2">{{cite web |title=Pešić otkrio: Jović i Pokuševski nisu dobili dozvolu |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2022&mm=08&dd=03&nav_id=2193359 |website=b92.net | date=8 March 2022 |access-date=3 August 2022}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Pokuševski's family originates from [[Priština]]. Due to the [[Kosovo War]] in 1999, his family escaped to [[Podgorica]] (nowadays in [[Montenegro]]), and moved to [[Belgrade]], [[Republic of Serbia (1992–2006)|Serbia]], afterwards, where Pokuševski was born in 2001. Thereafter, Pokuševski and his family permanently moved to [[Novi Sad]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Zapamtite ovo ime – Aleksej Pokuševski VIDEO|url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2019&mm=03&dd=19&nav_id=1519967|website=b92.net|date=19 March 2019|access-date=20 March 2019|language=sr}}</ref> Pokuševki's ancestors hail from [[Galicia (Eastern Europe)|Galicia]], present-day Ukraine.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ukrajino moja - Nedeljnik Vreme|url=https://www.vreme.com/vreme-uzivanja/ukrajino-moja/|website=Vreme.com|date=14 May 2014|access-date=8 May 2022|language=sr-RS}}</ref>

After signing a youth team contract with the Greek basketball club [[Olympiacos BC|Olympiacos]], Pokuševski moved to Greece in 2015, at the age of 13. While playing in Greek competitions, he counts as a native Greek domestic player, since he started competing in Greek competitions before the age of 14.<ref>[https://www.eurohoops.net/en/trademarks/994454/the-progress-card-of-10-european-nba-draft-prospects/11/ The progress card of 10 European NBA draft prospects.]</ref> He was eligible to represent either Serbia or Greece in national team competitions, and he chose to represent [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbia]].<ref name="nbacom">{{cite web|title=About Aleksej Pokusevski|url=https://www.nba.com/draft/2020/prospects/aleksej-pokusevski?ls=nba#/|website=NBA.com|access-date=24 June 2020}}</ref> His father Saša Pokuševski,<ref>[https://www.facebook.com/sasa.pokusevski Sasa Pokusevski.]</ref> is a former professional basketball player and a [[basketball coach|coach]]. His father played basketball with [[KB Prishtina|KK Priština]], and coached [[KK Novi Sad]].
